edit.description: `predicate_from_row`'s `when` arm (769-778) rebuilds the guard's row as `ClauseRow { predicate: guard_predicate_key, field: row.field.clone(), value_type: row.value_type.clone(), values: row.values.clone(), ..row.clone() }`. The spread carries `guard_predicate` through unchanged, so a row whose `guard_predicate` is itself `"when"` builds a guard row *identical to its input* and `predicate_from_row(&guard_row)` recurses forever — `temper check` aborts on a stack overflow where `contract.md` demands a loud refusal ("Guards do not nest"; "an unknown predicate is rejected at load, never skipped") and `compose.rs`'s own lift doc (196-198) promises "a corrupt lock rejected loud, never a clause silently dropped". Fix at the mechanism: the guard row is this row minus the `when` clause's own columns — `predicate` set to the guard key, `guard_predicate: None`, `body: None` — the read-side mirror of the writer's spread (`sdk/src/declarations.ts`'s `when` branch sets the clause's seven columns over the guard's row). A `when` guard then decodes to `None` at the inner `row.guard_predicate.as_deref()?` and `compose::clause_from_row` (412) refuses with `ClauseRowError::Predicate`, the existing corrupt-lock channel — no new error variant. The row format carries one `guard_predicate` column and one `body`, so this degenerate self-reference is the only way a lock can spell a nested guard at all; refusing it at lift closes the grammar rule on the read face. Drop the three explicit columns (`field`, `value_type`, `values`) in the same edit: `..row.clone()` already supplies them byte-for-byte, and naming three of the row's argument columns where the spread is total reads as the guard's special set — the partial-enumeration shape the write side shed in 395b5d78. The comment above the arm states the no-nesting rule and cites `contract.md`, "clause".

Add the refusal test beside `check_rejects_a_lock_clause_row_the_closed_vocabulary_cannot_admit` (1145), which is the same shape: a hand-built `Declarations` through `common::write_lock`, then `check_in`. Hand-authored input is correct here — a refusal test over a corruption the real writer cannot produce (`engineering.md`, "A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote": the real-writer bar scopes agreement claims only). The row is a `when` clause over a custom kind with `guard_predicate: Some("when")`, one `body` row, built with `..common::clause("when", "required")`. Assert the run fails and the output carries the corrupt-lock refusal naming the predicate — pre-fix the `check` child dies on SIGABRT (`check_in` spawns `CARGO_BIN_EXE_temper`, so the test binary survives), `ok` is false but the diagnostic assertion fails. The file's two existing guard-row sites need no change: `lock_quads` (2510-2519) reads a lifted `Predicate::When`'s guard target, and the 3527 lift builds its row with `predicate: "enum"` directly.

summary: A lock `when` row naming `when` as its own guard recurses forever: `check` aborts on a stack overflow where the grammar demands a loud corrupt-lock refusal.

tests.asserts: a committed lock whose `when` clause row names `when` as its own `guard_predicate` makes `check` fail loud with the corrupt-lock refusal naming the predicate, never abort

acceptance: `cargo test` green with the new refusal test — which fails on the pre-fix tree, where the `check` child aborts with `fatal runtime error: stack overflow` and prints no refusal; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.
notes: Probed on disk this tick: a real harness lock plus one `when` row with `guard_predicate = "when"` makes `temper check` abort — `thread 'main' has overflowed its stack`, exit 134. `engine.rs`'s `when_restrictions` (236-262) already holds both grammar rules, guard set and no-nesting, and is simply downstream of the lift that dies. Found by the post-ship sweep of the read half of the seam 395b5d78 respelled. scoped at dcec6f98
